memory_candidates.content: In this repo's agent-system extension layout, an extension's manifest.json provides.scripts array is a deployment ALLOWLIST, not documentation: the loader copies only the enumerated scripts flat into .claude/scripts/, and check-extension-docs.sh Rule E (check_referenced_scripts_declared) fails on a script referenced in docs but absent from the array. Any task whose file_scope adds a NEW script under agent-system/extensions/*/scripts/ therefore has an implicit fifth file — the manifest entry — without which the new script never deploys and the change is inert at runtime, while still looking complete in the source store. Plans that add a new extension script should treat the manifest entry as part of the same phase as the script itself, so the script is deployable at its own commit boundary.

In bash scripts running `set -euo pipefail`, a `VAR="$(cmd1 | grep -oP 'pattern' | head -1)"` pipeline silently aborts the WHOLE SCRIPT when grep finds zero matches (grep exits 1 on no-match, and pipefail propagates that through the pipeline, and set -e then kills the script at the assignment). This is a second, easy-to-miss failure mode distinct from "the called command itself might fail" — it bit a capture-guarded helper invocation whose OWN exit was already guarded with `|| VAR=""`, because the guard was only on the helper call, not on a downstream grep-based parsing pipeline applied to its output. Any downstream `grep`/`head`/`tail` pipeline built on a value that might legitimately be empty or non-matching needs its own `|| VAR=""` guard, verified live via a forced-failure test (renaming the dependency) rather than reasoned about in the abstract.
